title: Discrete time crystals and classical logic gates in coupled open Dicke models
authors: Emmanuel D. G. U, Roy D. Jara, Jayson G. Cosme
abstract: We investigate the dynamics of coupled discrete time crystals (DTCs) in the coupled Dicke model or Dicke dimer (DD) with dissipation. By numerically simulating the mean-field dynamics of the system, we show that coupling two DTCs decreases their oscillation amplitude following a transient relaxation period. For sufficiently strong coupling, the coupled DTCs become unstable, resulting in the system relaxing towards the normal phase (NP). We demonstrate that the relaxation time diverges near the critical coupling strength, suggesting a continuous phase transition. Using the truncated Wigner approximation (TWA), we explore how the dynamics are affected by the introduction of quantum fluctuations. We also consider a scenario in which an NP is briefly coupled to a DTC, seeding the NP to transform into a DTC that is either synchronized or anti-synchronized relative to the DTC. We investigate the robustness of this phenomenon in the presence of noise. Using these results, we propose a scheme to perform NAND and NOR operations with three DTCs by sequentially coupling the input and output sites. We identify the parameter regimes in which the logic gate architecture remains valid, and investigate how the protocol is affected by the presence of quantum fluctuations.
summary: This paper studies coupled Discrete Time Crystals (DTCs) in the Dicke model, analyzing their dynamics under coupling and dissipation. The authors show that DTCs can be manipulated to perform classical logic operations (NAND/NOR) by implementing a protocol of sequential pulsed coupling. This work suggests that engineered quantum many-body systems can serve as robust, physical building blocks for quantum information processing.
main_problem: The paper investigates the dynamics of coupled Discrete Time Crystals (DTCs) and proposes using these physical systems to implement classical logic gates like NAND and NOR.
main_result: A protocol for implementing NAND and NOR gates is demonstrated using three coupled DTCs, showing that the logic operation is robust within specific parameter regimes.
method: The dynamics are analyzed using mean-field simulations derived from the Lindblad master equation, supplemented by the Truncated Wigner Approximation (TWA) to account for quantum fluctuations.
model_or_system: The system is based on the coupled Dicke model (or Dicke dimer) involving bosonic and spin operators, exhibiting DTC phases characterized by broken discrete time translation symmetry.
key_observables: DTC response amplitude ($A_r$), relaxation time ($	au_r$), final phase difference ($\Delta\phi_f$), and the probability of achieving a valid logic gate ($P_{	ext{Valid}}$).
important_parameters: Coupling strength ($J$), dissipation ($\kappa$), and pulse durations ($T_q$ or $T_{1O}$), relative to critical coupling strengths ($J_{c,FM}, J_{c,AFM}$).
main_assumptions: The use of the Truncated Wigner Approximation (TWA) to map the master equation to effective stochastic equations, and the assumption that sequential pulsed coupling can reliably reset and operate the logic gates.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of amplitudes and phase differences during coupling, show power-law scaling of relaxation times near critical points, and map out the parameter space required for successful NAND/NOR gate operations.
paper_structure: The paper first analyzes the general dynamics of coupled DTCs, identifying phase transitions and the effect of coupling. It then details the use of pulsed coupling to control the final state (synchronization/anti-synchronization) and culminates in proposing and verifying the NAND/NOR logic gate architecture.
why_interesting: This work bridges fundamental condensed matter physics (DTCs, open quantum systems) with quantum information processing, demonstrating a physical platform for quantum computation using non-equilibrium dynamics.
